verdict: Avoid new unsecured or thinly-collateralised exposure to Sivakasi fireworks and match units; lend only to the few large, low-geared, advance-funded manufacturers with clean green-cracker approvals, and only on tight cash-flow structures.
title: Sivakasi fireworks & safety matches: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
Cash sits in finished stock and in dealer receivables, not in the plant. **Manufacturing cost has risen 15-25 per cent this year on aluminium powder and colour salts [1], and several smaller units have already shut [1].** So when a proposal lands, check the raw-material cost pass-through clause in the order book; if pricing is fixed for the season, ask how the 15-25 per cent cost rise is absorbed. ## Where cash and value actually sit
**The peer rating file shows collection periods of 302 days in FY21, 236 in FY22 and 182 in FY23, improving only because green-cracker orders were booked against advance [10].** That is the whole credit story: the good borrower is the one who has moved from extended dealer credit to advance. **The same file shows gearing of 0.03x and interest cover of 17.72x in FY21, supported by free cash of ₹81.68 crore [9]** — but that is a large, old, dated balance sheet, so treat it as a benchmark, not a template. For any Sivakasi proposal, collect from customer the current receivable days, advance share of order book and gearing; if receivable days exceed the FY23 peer level of 182 [10], ask for the dealer-wise ageing and the security behind it. ## What has broken now
**This season has cost inflation, labour shortage, unseasonal rain and a delayed Supreme Court ruling on green crackers all at once [1].** Sattur recorded 143 mm of rain on 22 October [3], which hits drying and filling schedules. **Tamil Nadu GST collections are down 3.2 per cent Apr-to-date against India's +6.1 per cent [D], and IIP for NIC 20 is -0.5 per cent YoY with -1.2 per cent Apr-to-date [D].** Bank credit is running +20.7 per cent YoY against that output fall [D], so the system is lending into a shrinking output base. Note the local sources are current (31 October 2026) but the rating files [9][10] are undated and old; the peer IT articles [4][5] are irrelevant to this industry and should be ignored. ## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue the large, compliant manufacturers who have green-cracker approvals and are booking orders against advance [2][10].** The relaxation for joined green crackers [2] is the real growth line — lend to units investing in that line and in automation, not to traders. **Avoid the small units that have already shown they cannot absorb the 15-25 per cent cost rise [1], and avoid pure dealer-financing against festive stock.** Structure as cash-flow lending against confirmed orders, with advance receipts escrowed, a stock-and-receivables charge, and a covenant that receivable days stay at or below the FY23 peer level of 182 [10]. Take monthly stock statements, monthly advance-receipt register and quarterly GST returns; if GST turnover trails the stock statement, stop fresh disbursement. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch the order book shifting from advance to credit, rain days in October-November, and any adverse green-cracker ruling.** If advance share of orders falls below the prior year, ask for the dealer list and reduce limit. If Sattur-type rainfall repeats [3], ask for the production-loss estimate before the season closes. If the Supreme Court ruling slips again [1], ask for the contingency plan on unsold stock.
